The test `test_isocalendar_returns_correct_values_close_to_new_year_with_tz()` checks whether the `isocalendar` method of a DatetimeIndex correctly returns the year, week, and day according to the ISO 8601 standard. However, the test fails with an error message indicating that ExtensionArray values are different.

Upon examining the execution path of this test, we find that it calls the `isocalendar` method on a DatetimeIndex object created from dates near the new year (December 29-31, 2013) with time zone Europe/Brussels. The method returns a DataFrame where columns "year", "week", and "day" are of type UInt32.

The error occurs because the expected result has different values in the "year" column for December 30 and 31: [2013, 2014] vs. [2014, 2014]. This discrepancy likely arises from the time zone handling when calculating the week number.

Following this reasoning, it appears that there is an issue with time zone conversion or normalization when computing the ISO week numbers close to the start of a new year in the specified time zone.
